title: Nasruddin Tale 168: The Borrowed Donkey Saddle
summary: A neighbor loaned Nasruddin a leather saddle. Whenever they met in the bazaar, the neighbor shouted loudly: "Look at Nasruddin riding so comfortably upon my leather saddle!"...
full_text:
A neighbor loaned Nasruddin a leather saddle. Whenever they met in the bazaar, the neighbor shouted loudly: "Look at Nasruddin riding so comfortably upon my leather saddle!"

Tired of the public boasting, Nasruddin took the saddle off in the middle of the crowded square, placed it on the neighbor's shoulders, and walked away leading his bare-backed donkey: "Now ride your own saddle through the bazaar, and let the town see who carries the true burden!"
moral: Constantly reminding others of a small favor destroys the value of the gift.
